title: 第七章 夜磨
content_zh:
日子在砍柴、挑水、清理杂草的循环中，又翻过了七八页。

    陈默的柴刀越来越亮，在晨光中挥砍时，偶尔能反射出一线刺眼的冷光。磨刀的三块石头，表面也被磨出了清晰的凹痕，尤其是那块最细腻的深色石头，中心处已微微下陷，光滑如镜。那把断剑的锈迹，也被他耐心地磨掉了一小片，露出底下布满黑色斑点的铁质，但终究是凡铁，又锈蚀得太深，难堪大用，最后被他磨成了一根两头尖锐的粗糙铁锥，偶尔用来撬撬石头，或是在木头上钻个眼。

    体术残篇的第一个动作，他已经能勉强维持十五息。每多坚持一息，肩臂和背部的筋肉都像被重新撕裂一遍，但那种深入筋腱骨髓的拉伸感过后，往往会带来一丝极其微弱的、仿佛淤塞被稍稍冲开的通畅感。配合着每隔几日、谨慎服用的微量铁骨草汁液（他再也不敢像第一次那样莽撞），他感觉自己的筋骨似乎真的比以往强韧了那么一丝。至少，在背负沉重柴捆下山时，脚步似乎稳了分毫。

    那几朵品相不佳的雾灵菇，被他放在通风处阴干了。他没敢再吃，只是偶尔拿在手里闻闻那股清凉的气息，试图让自己纷杂的思绪平静下来。炼气吐纳依旧艰难，胸口那堵“墙”坚如磐石，暖流每日冲击，却只能让其盘桓的时间从三十息缓慢增加到三十五息，再难寸进。他知道，这是瓶颈。对于四灵根而言，每一个小关卡，都可能卡住无数人一辈子。

    外门小比的日子越来越近。杂役院里，关于小比的议论也多了起来，虽然大多数人只是嘴上说说。王虎彻底熄了心思，每日只是麻木地完成分内的活计，然后便躺在铺位上发呆。倒是那个曾一起清理杂草的李大，似乎心有不甘，时常拉着人打听小比的细节，说什么“就算去走个过场，见见世面也好”。

    陈默没有参与这些议论。他依旧严格按照那张日课纸生活。只是在夜深人静，完成所有修炼后，他会拿出那本周安执事的丹药笔记，就着如豆的灯火（他如今每隔五六日，会舍得点上半时辰油灯），反复研读前面关于基础草药矿物辨识、炮制的内容。那些字句早已烂熟于心，但他仍看得仔细，仿佛要从那些平淡的描述里，榨取出每一分可能对他有用的信息。

    他注意到笔记中多次提到“杂质”二字。无论是低劣草药，还是普通矿石，杂质多是效力微弱、甚至有害的根源。如何用最简陋的方法去除杂质，是笔记前半部分反复探讨的重点。比如铁骨草，笔记提到，若有条件，应以山泉水反复浸泡、捶打、过滤，取其最精华的汁液，可大幅减少对肠胃的刺激和无效杂质的摄入。又比如青礞石，需反复淘洗、沉淀，取最细腻的粉末，方能发挥些许“静心宁神”之效，否则反易令人心浮气躁。

    这些方法，对如今的陈默而言，大多是可望不可及。山泉水好说，但反复浸泡捶打需要时间和容器，过滤需要细布，这些他都缺乏。淘洗青礞石，需要水盆和耐心，在杂役院众目睽睽之下，也难以进行。

    但他记下了。记在了心里，也记在了日课纸的背面。与那些关于气感运行、体术练习的记录混杂在一起，形成了他独有的、旁人看来或许毫无价值的修行日志。

    这日午后，陈默被派去整理杂役院的旧库房。库房在院子的最西头，是一间低矮阴暗的土坯房，平日里堆放些破损的农具、淘汰的旧物，少有人来。管事赵胖子叼着根草茎，含糊地交代：“把里头能用的家伙什理出来，锈得太厉害的、烂透的，扔到后头废料堆去。弄干净点，过几日宗门可能要清点。”

    推开吱呀作响的木门，一股浓重的霉味和铁锈味扑面而来。库房里很暗，只有高处一个小窗透进些许天光，照亮空气中飞舞的尘埃。地上、墙边堆满了各种杂物：缺了口的犁头，散了架的木轮，锈成一团的铁链，破旧的箩筐，还有一堆看不清原样的废旧金属。

    陈默挽起袖子，开始清理。他先将那些完全腐烂的木质家具拖出去，又将一些破损到无法修补的陶罐瓦盆清理到一边。然后，他开始整理那些金属工具。

    大多是生铁打造的寻常农具，锈蚀严重。他拿起一把几乎锈穿的柴刀，比了比自己怀里那把，摇了摇头，将其扔到废弃的那堆。又拿起一把豁口比锯子还多的镰刀，同样丢弃。

    清理到墙角时，他的脚碰到一个沉甸甸的、用破麻袋盖着的东西。他掀开麻袋，下面是一堆黑乎乎、大小不一的金属块，看起来像是某些大型器械上拆卸下来的零件，或者冶炼失败的铁疙瘩。大多锈得厉害，形状也不规则。

    陈默本打算将其一并归入废料。但当他随手拿起一块巴掌大、入手格外沉重的铁块时，指尖传来的触感和重量，让他动作顿了顿。

    这块铁颜色深黑，锈迹相对较少，表面粗糙，布满蜂窝状的细孔，但质地异常坚硬沉重。他用力掰了掰，纹丝不动。又捡起另一块废铁敲了敲，声音沉闷，不像普通生铁。

    他心中微动，想起周安笔记中，曾简单提到过几种低阶炼器材料，其中有一种叫“黑铁”，描述是“色深黑，质密而沉，凡火难熔，低阶法器胚体常用辅料，然杂质极多，提纯不易”。

    难道这是黑铁？他不敢确定。笔记上只有文字描述，并无图形。而且就算是，以他如今的条件，也根本无法熔炼提纯。

    但他还是将这块沉重的铁块，单独放到了一边。接着，他又在破烂堆里翻找，陆陆续续，又找出三四块质地、颜色、重量类似的金属块，大小不一，其中一块有脸盆大小，扁扁的，边缘不规则，但一面相对平整。

    陈默看着这几块黑乎乎的铁疙瘩，想了想，将那块脸盆大、一面平整的，和另一块较小的、形状较规整的，用破麻袋片裹好，藏在了库房一个不起眼的、堆着干草的角落。剩下的，则归入了待处理的废料。
content_en:
The days passed by another seven or eight pages in the cycle of chopping firewood, carrying water, and clearing weeds.
Chen Mo's hatchet became brighter and brighter. When he slashed in the morning light, it occasionally reflected a dazzling cold light.The three stones used for sharpening the knife also had clear indentations on their surfaces, especially the most delicate dark stone, which had sunken slightly in the center and was as smooth as a mirror.He also patiently rubbed off a small piece of the rust on the broken sword, revealing the iron underneath which was covered with black spots. But it was ordinary iron after all, and the rust was too deep to be useful. Finally, he ground it into a rough iron awl with sharp ends, which he occasionally used to pry stones or drill holes in wood.
In the first movement of the fragmentary chapter of physical skills, he could barely maintain fifteen breaths.With every extra breath, the muscles in the shoulders, arms and back feel like they are being torn apart all over again, but after that stretch that goes deep into the tendons and marrow, there is often an extremely weak sense of smoothness, as if a blockage has been slightly washed away.Coupled with the careful consumption of trace amounts of Iron Bone Grass juice every few days (he never dared to be as reckless as the first time), he felt that his muscles and bones seemed to be a little stronger than before.At least, my steps seemed to be steady as I carried the heavy bundle of firewood down the mountain.
The few mist mushrooms that were not in good condition were placed in a ventilated place to dry in the shade.He didn't dare to eat anymore, but occasionally held it in his hand and smelled the cool breath, trying to calm down his complicated thoughts.Refining Qi and breathing out is still difficult, the "wall" in the chest is as solid as a rock, and the warm current hits it every day, but it can only slowly increase the time it lingers from thirty breaths to thirty-five breaths, and it is difficult to make any further progress.He knew that this was the bottleneck.For the Four Spiritual Roots, every small level may block countless people for a lifetime.
The day of the outer door is getting closer and closer.In the courtyard, there were more talks about Xiao Bi, although most people only talked about it.Wang Hu completely lost his mind and just completed his assigned tasks numbly every day, and then lay on the bunk in a daze.On the other hand, Li Da, who we had worked with to clean up weeds, seemed unwilling to do so. He often asked people to inquire about the details of Xiao Bi, saying, "It's just a formality to see the world."
Chen Mo did not participate in these discussions.He still lives strictly according to the daily schedule.But in the dead of night, after completing all the training, he would take out Deacon Zhou An's elixir notes, and by the light of Rudou (he would light an oil lamp for half an hour every five or six days now), he would repeatedly study the previous content on the identification and preparation of basic herbal medicines and minerals.Those words were already familiar by heart, but he still read them carefully, as if he wanted to squeeze out every bit of information that might be useful to him from those plain descriptions.
He noticed that the word "impurity" was mentioned many times in the notes.Whether it is inferior herbs or ordinary minerals, impurities are often the source of weak effectiveness or even harmful effects.How to use the simplest method to remove impurities is the focus of repeated discussion in the first half of the note.For example, the notes mention that if conditions permit, it should be repeatedly soaked, beaten, and filtered in mountain spring water to extract the most essence of the juice, which can greatly reduce gastrointestinal irritation and the intake of ineffective impurities.Another example is Qingmao Stone, which needs to be washed and precipitated repeatedly to obtain the finest powder before it can exert some "calming and calming" effect. Otherwise, it will easily make people feel restless.
Most of these methods are out of reach for Chen Mo today.Mountain spring water is easy to talk about, but repeated soaking and beating requires time and containers, and filtering requires fine cloth, both of which he lacks.Washing the bluestone requires a basin and patience, and it is difficult to do it in full view of the public.
But he remembered it.I remembered it in my heart and also wrote it down on the back of the daily lesson paper.Mixed with the records about the movement of Qi and physical skills, it formed his unique practice diary, which may seem worthless to others.
In the afternoon of this day, Chen Mo was sent to clean up the old warehouse in the courtyard.The warehouse is at the western end of the yard. It is a low and dark adobe house. It is usually stocked with broken farm tools and obsolete old things, and few people come here.The steward, Fatty Zhao, held a piece of grass in his mouth and said vaguely: "Take out the usable ones from inside. Throw the ones that are too rusty and rotten into the scrap pile at the back. Keep them clean. The sect may have to take inventory in a few days."
Pushing open the creaking wooden door, a strong smell of musty and rust hit my face.The warehouse was very dark, with only a small window high up letting in some light, illuminating the dust flying in the air.The floor and walls were filled with all kinds of debris: chipped plowshares, broken wooden wheels, rusted iron chains, worn baskets, and a pile of scrap metal whose original condition could not be clearly seen.
Chen Mo rolled up his sleeves and started cleaning.He first dragged out the completely rotted wooden furniture, and then cleaned aside some clay pots and pots that were damaged beyond repair.Then he began to sort out the metal tools.
Most of them are ordinary farm tools made of pig iron and are severely rusted.He picked up a hatchet that was almost rusted through, gestured to the one in his arms, shook his head, and threw it into the discarded pile.He picked up a sickle with more gaps than a saw and discarded it as well.
When he reached the corner of the wall, his feet came across a heavy object covered with a torn sack.He opened the sack, and underneath was a pile of black metal blocks of different sizes. They looked like disassembled parts from some large equipment, or iron lumps that had failed to be smelted.Most were badly rusted and irregular in shape.
Chen Mo originally planned to put it into scrap.But when he casually picked up a piece of iron that was as big as a palm and extremely heavy, the touch and weight from his fingertips made him pause.
This piece of iron is dark black in color with relatively little rust. Its surface is rough and covered with honeycomb-like pores, but its texture is extremely hard and heavy.He broke it off hard, but it didn't move at all.He picked up another piece of scrap iron and knocked it. The sound was dull, not like ordinary pig iron.
His heart moved slightly, and he remembered that Zhou An briefly mentioned several low-level weapon-making materials in his notes, one of which was called "black iron", which was described as "deep black in color, dense and heavy in quality, refractory to ordinary fire, and commonly used auxiliary materials for low-level magic weapon embryos. However, there are many impurities, making it difficult to purify."
Is this black iron?He wasn't sure.There are only text descriptions in the notes, no graphics.And even if it were, with his current conditions, it would be impossible to smelt and purify it.
But he still put the heavy piece of iron aside alone.Then, he rummaged through the junk pile, and one after another, he found three or four metal blocks of similar texture, color, and weight, varying in size. One of them was the size of a washbasin, flat, with irregular edges, but one side was relatively flat.
Chen Mo looked at these dark iron lumps, thought for a moment, and wrapped the one with a large basin and a flat side and the other with a smaller one and a more regular shape in broken sacks and hid them in an inconspicuous corner of the warehouse where hay was piled.The rest is classified as waste to be processed.
